newsitem.title: CANADA: United Grain jumps on takeover offer.
newsitem.headline: United Grain jumps on takeover offer.

text.p: Shares in United Grain Growers Ltd (UGG) soared on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Thursday after two grain handling rivals launched a C$172 million takeover bid for the Winnipeg-based company.

UGG's stock jumped 1.50 to a 52-week high of 14.00 on Canada's largest stock market. The stock was trading higher than the C$13.75 per share bid launched by Alberta Wheat Pool and Manitoba Pool Elevators earlier today.
"If it is trading above the bid price it means people feel (UGG's) value not fully represented in the offer," said Ira Katzin, an investment advisor at RBC Dominion Securities.
A UGG executive said on Thursday the company's board of directors will study the takeover offer.
"The board will need time to assess the adequacy and terms of the offer and we will make a statement when they've had time to do that," said UGG chief executive officer Brian Hayward.
The bid is conditional on UGG waiving a poison pill provision put in place by its board on February 14 and other conditions, including no adverse change in UGG's businesses.
